body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **6.2** to **7.10.7**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs
  explaining the specific message.  Closes `issue 1921`_.

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2048


.. _changes_7-10-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.6
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses
  that ran in different directories, as reported in `issue 1499`_.  This is now
  fixed.

- Performance: `Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning <pull 2038_>`_ the speed of
  combination, especially with many contexts.

.. _issue 1499: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1499
.. _pull 2038: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2038


.. _changes_7-10-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Big speed improvements for ``coverage combine``: it's now about twice as
  fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests `2032 <pull 2032_>`_,
  `2033 <pull 2033_>`_, and `2034 <pull 2034_>`_.

.. _pull 2032: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2032
.. _pull 2033: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2033
.. _pull 2034: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2034


.. _changes_7-10-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added ``patch = fork`` for times when the built-in forking support is
  insufficient.

- Fix: ``patch = execv`` also inherits the entire coverage configuration now.


.. _changes_7-10-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fixes for ``patch = subprocess``:

  - If subprocesses spawned yet more subprocesses simultaneously, some coverage
    could be missed.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2024`_.

  - If subprocesses were created in other directories, their data files were
    stranded there and not combined into the totals, as described in `issue
    2025`_.  This is now fixed.

  - On Windows (or maybe only some Windows?) the patch would fail with a
    ``ModuleNotFound`` error trying to import coverage.  This is now fixed,
    closing `issue 2022`_.

  - Originally only options set in the coverage configuration file would apply
    to subprocesses.  Options set on the ``coverage run`` command line (such as
    ``--branch``) wouldn't be communicated to the subprocesses.  This could
    lead to combining failures, as described in `issue 2021`_. Now the entire
    configuration is used in subprocesses, regardless of its origin.

  - Added ``debug=patch`` to help diagnose problems.

- Fix: really close all SQLite databases, even in-memory ones. Closes `issue
  2017`_.

.. _issue 2017: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2017
.. _issue 2021: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2021
.. _issue 2022: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2022
.. _issue 2024: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2024
.. _issue 2025: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2025


.. _changes_7-10-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some code with NOP bytecodes could report missing branches that are
  actually executed. This is now fixed, closing `issue 1999`_. Python 3.9
  still shows the problem.

.. _issue 1999: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1999


.. _changes_7-10-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the exclusion for ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` was wrong: it marked the branch
  as partial, but it should have been a line exclusion so the entire clause
  would be excluded. Improves `issue 831`_.

- Fix: changed where .pth files are written for ``patch = subprocess``, closing
  `issue 2006`_.

.. _issue 2006: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2006


.. _changes_7-10-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_, its duplicate `issue 378`_ and old
    `issue 689`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes
  `issue 831`_.

- A new command-line option: ``--save-signal=USR1`` specifies a signal that
  coverage.py will listen for.  When the signal is sent, the coverage data will
  be saved.  This makes it possible to save data from within long-running
  processes.  Thanks, `Arkady Gilinsky <pull 1998_>`_.

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_report_partial_also`" is a list of
  regexes to add as pragmas for partial branches.  This parallels the
  ":ref:`config_report_exclude_also`" setting for adding line exclusion
  patterns.

- A few file path configuration settings didn't allow for tilde expansion:
  :ref:`config_json_output`, :ref:`config_lcov_output` and
  :ref:`config_run_debug_file`.  This is now fixed.

- Wheels are included for 3.14 now that 3.14 rc1 is available.

- We no longer ship a PyPy-specific wheel. PyPy will install the pure-Python
  wheel.  Closes `issue 2001`_.

- In the very unusual situation of not having a current frame, coverage no
  longer crashes when using the sysmon core, fixing `issue 2005`_.

# Storm Water Infrastructure Management System

## Overview

This pull request introduces two sophisticated smart contracts that form the backbone of a decentralized neighborhood storm water management system. Built on Stacks blockchain using Clarity, these contracts enable transparent coordination of green infrastructure projects, maintenance scheduling, and flood prevention initiatives.

## Smart Contracts Implemented

### 1. Infrastructure Planning Contract (`infrastructure-planning.clar`)

**Purpose**: Manages the complete lifecycle of green infrastructure projects from proposal to implementation, including community voting, resource allocation, and environmental impact assessment.

**Key Features**:
- **Stakeholder Management**: Comprehensive registration system for community members, authorities, and environmental organizations
- **Democratic Project Proposal**: Community-driven project submissions with transparent voting mechanisms
- **Budget Management**: Automated budget allocation and tracking for approved projects
- **Milestone Tracking**: Project progress monitoring with timeline and budget oversight
- **Environmental Assessment**: Systematic evaluation of environmental impact and benefits
- **Voting Power Management**: Flexible voting systems accommodating different stakeholder expertise levels

**Core Functions**:
- `register-stakeholder`: Register community participants with expertise and contact information
- `submit-project-proposal`: Submit infrastructure projects with comprehensive specifications
- `vote-on-project`: Democratic voting system with weighted stakeholder input
- `finalize-project-voting`: Automated project approval based on community consensus
- `add-project-milestone`: Project milestone tracking with budget allocation
- `record-environmental-assessment`: Environmental impact documentation and scoring

### 2. Maintenance Scheduling Contract (`maintenance-scheduling.clar`)

**Purpose**: Comprehensive system for scheduling maintenance tasks, coordinating volunteers, managing equipment inventory, and monitoring infrastructure performance.

**Key Features**:
- **Volunteer Coordination**: Registration and skill-based task assignment system
- **Task Management**: Create, assign, and track maintenance activities with priority levels
- **Equipment Inventory**: Complete equipment tracking and allocation system
- **Performance Monitoring**: Infrastructure health tracking and reporting
- **Availability Scheduling**: Volunteer availability management and automated scheduling
- **Skill Verification**: Task assignment based on required skills and experience levels

While working locally on packaging a recipe depending on `libxau`, I encountered this error:

```bash
> rm -rf /tmp/output; brioche build -o /tmp/output -p packages/libxmu
 INFO build:bake:bake_process:bake_process_finalize: brioche_core::bake::process: keeping temporary bake dir /home/jaudiger.linux/.local/share/brioche/process-temp/01K5R8FE8S8XN895QXMF4E7A3S recipe_hash=f020ed4de0a4c94b88766c6bf748c99fdc7687f222998216ad1e3b85af764bc1 bake_dir=/home/jaudiger.linux/.local/share/brioche/process-temp/01K5R8FE8S8XN895QXMF4E7A3S
63791  │   CCLD     libXmu.la
       │ libtool: warning: library '/home/brioche-runner-f020ed4de0a4c94b88766c6bf748c99fdc7687f222998216ad1e3b85af764bc1/.local/share/brioche/locals/d3fa41bf6228de8d413fc70cf052e2c696904b478e31e27fa90ea311c018f632/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib/libXt.la' was moved.
       │ grep: E.la: invalid context length argument
       │ libtool:   error: '-lICE.la' is not a valid libtool archive
       │ make[2]: Leaving directory '/home/brioche-runner-f020ed4de0a4c94b88766c6bf748c99fdc7687f222998216ad1e3b85af764bc1/work/src'
       │ make[2]: *** [Makefile:542: libXmu.la] Error 1
       │ make[1]: Leaving directory '/home/brioche-runner-f020ed4de0a4c94b88766c6bf748c99fdc7687f222998216ad1e3b85af764bc1/work'
       │ make[1]: *** [Makefile:495: all-recursive] Error 1
       │ make: *** [Makefile:402: all] Error 2
 7.88s ◞ Process 63791
```

While I understood the error, I was surprised to see `-lICE.la` instead of `-lICE`.

The culprit was coming from this file:

```bash
cat /tmp/output/lib/libXt.la
# libXt.la - a libtool library file
# Generated by libtool (GNU libtool) 2.4.7
#
# Please DO NOT delete this file!
# It is necessary for linking the library.

# The name that we can dlopen(3).
dlname='libXt.so.6'

# Names of this library.
library_names='libXt.so.6.0.0 libXt.so.6 libXt.so'

# The name of the static archive.
old_library='libXt.a'

# Linker flags that cannot go in dependency_libs.
inherited_linker_flags=''

# Libraries that this one depends upon.
dependency_libs=' -L/home/brioche-runner-adbd734b8c42bd92a4d2721221745f5073588e578b9677e937e37e265c5e08f0/.local/share/brioche/locals/297d40f66c73f4d12e4cebc1f9410e17f7049c64307cfefe7fc490f8451e67a5/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib //lib/libSM.la -L/home/brioche-runner-cd1a0db1d7c6c1aac7b9bbfeb706e67be7e8660f531104cb31545292b17e57c7/.local/share/brioche/locals/1c747857a1af338c123a33c763b8c881c1287ae25f7749500fa89931529b979c/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib -lICE -L/home/brioche-runner-cd1a0db1d7c6c1aac7b9bbfeb706e67be7e8660f531104cb31545292b17e57c7/.local/share/brioche/locals/ac72c24ec53721f2b9012665360657d3996993f9405f05cbdf05ede7ecf28526/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib -luuid //lib/libICE.la //lib/libuuid.la -L/home/brioche-runner-adbd734b8c42bd92a4d2721221745f5073588e578b9677e937e37e265c5e08f0/.local/share/brioche/locals/1c747857a1af338c123a33c763b8c881c1287ae25f7749500fa89931529b979c/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib //lib/libICE.la -L/home/brioche-runner-adbd734b8c42bd92a4d2721221745f5073588e578b9677e937e37e265c5e08f0/.local/share/brioche/locals/bdb83b53b61db082a604a1c92e470e57998902fc738af3fcfa78c44b6a2daedb/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib //lib/libX11.la -L/home/brioche-runner-1fd16e875521eb53e2594c66fa6f1ad87d99e170789360b957f271f1c558ec86/.local/share/brioche/locals/6336d0eae785f3b671549410c217cd697e1f52f858c59f8f80d43f6b0b47f7cd/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib -lxcb -L/home/brioche-runner-7a3bad84e147aa8383556681d27280715221e4837641672ac9c5b4e9abf368c1/.local/share/brioche/locals/7030701dd55d14702c05c7382ff7ab39d84601640d2c4a06e5d15660083564b7/lib/pkgconfig/../../lib -lpthread //lib/libxcb.la -lXau //lib/libXau.la'

# Names of additional weak libraries provided by this library
weak_library_names=''

# Version information for libXt.
current=6
age=0
revision=0

# Is this an already installed library?
installed=yes

# Should we warn about portability when linking against -modules?
shouldnotlink=no

# Files to dlopen/dlpreopen
dlopen=''
dlpreopen=''

# Directory that this library needs to be installed in:
libdir='//lib'
```

So, after having checked a first time `std.libtoolSanitizeDependencies()`, I didn't see any easy issue to resolve. The regex was working for most of the recipes, but a few ones were not updated.

Then, I discovered [this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/26396986/what-is-the-special-character-escape-for-whitespace-in-a-posix-extented-regu?utm_source=chatgpt.com) which states that `\s` is not POSIX and is not well handled by sed. For proper whitespace detection, we should use `:space:` (this one is POSIX compliant). And indeed after updating the regex, it worked, and my recipe depending on `libxau` was working:

```bash
> cat /tmp/output/lib/libXt.la

### Update [requests](https://pypi.org/project/requests) from **2.28.2** to **2.32.5**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.32.5
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**

- The SSLContext caching feature originally introduced in 2.32.0 has created
  a new class of issues in Requests that have had negative impact across a number
  of use cases. The Requests team has decided to revert this feature as long term
  maintenance of it is proving to be unsustainable in its current iteration.

**Deprecations**
- Added support for Python 3.14.
- Dropped support for Python 3.8 following its end of support.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.4
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- CVE-2024-47081 Fixed an issue where a maliciously crafted URL and trusted
  environment will retrieve credentials for the wrong hostname/machine from a
  netrc file.

**Improvements**
- Numerous documentation improvements

**Deprecations**
- Added support for pypy 3.11 for Linux and macOS.
- Dropped support for pypy 3.9 following its end of support.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.3
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug breaking the ability to specify custom SSLContexts in sub-classes of
  HTTPAdapter. (6716)
- Fixed issue where Requests started failing to run on Python versions compiled
  without the `ssl` module. (6724)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.2
   ```
   -------------------

**Deprecations**
- To provide a more stable migration for custom HTTPAdapters impacted
  by the CVE changes in 2.32.0, we've renamed `_get_connection` to
  a new public API, `get_connection_with_tls_context`. Existing custom
  HTTPAdapters will need to migrate their code to use this new API.
  `get_connection` is considered deprecated in all versions of Requests>=2.32.0.

  A minimal (2-line) example has been provided in the linked PR to ease
  migration, but we strongly urge users to evaluate if their custom adapter
  is subject to the same issue described in CVE-2024-35195. (6710)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Add missing test certs to the sdist distributed on PyPI.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Fixed an issue where setting `verify=False` on the first request from a
  Session will cause subsequent requests to the _same origin_ to also ignore
  cert verification, regardless of the value of `verify`.
  (https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56)

**Improvements**
- `verify=True` now reuses a global SSLContext which should improve
  request time variance between first and subsequent requests. It should
  also minimize certificate load time on Windows systems when using a Python
  version built with OpenSSL 3.x. (6667)
- Requests now supports optional use of character detection
  (`chardet` or `charset_normalizer`) when repackaged or vendored.
  This enables `pip` and other projects to minimize their vendoring
  surface area. The `Response.text()` and `apparent_encoding` APIs
  will default to `utf-8` if neither library is present. (6702)

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug in length detection where emoji length was incorrectly
  calculated in the request content-length. (6589)
- Fixed deserialization bug in JSONDecodeError. (6629)
- Fixed bug where an extra leading `/` (path separator) could lead
  urllib3 to unnecessarily reparse the request URI. (6644)

**Deprecations**

- Requests has officially added support for CPython 3.12 (6503)
- Requests has officially added support for PyPy 3.9 and 3.10 (6641)
- Requests has officially dropped support for CPython 3.7 (6642)
- Requests has officially dropped support for PyPy 3.7 and 3.8 (6641)

**Documentation**
- Various typo fixes and doc improvements.

**Packaging**
- Requests has started adopting some modern packaging practices.
  The source files for the projects (formerly `requests`) is now located
  in `src/requests` in the Requests sdist. (6506)
- Starting in Requests 2.33.0, Requests will migrate to a PEP 517 build system
  using `hatchling`. This should not impact the average user, but extremely old
  versions of packaging utilities may have issues with the new packaging format.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.31.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Versions of Requests between v2.3.0 and v2.30.0 are vulnerable to potential
  forwarding of `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers when
  following HTTPS redirects.

  When proxies are defined with user info (`https://user:passproxy:8080`), Requests
  will construct a `Proxy-Authorization` header that is attached to the request to
  authenticate with the proxy.

  In cases where Requests receives a redirect response, it previously reattached
  the `Proxy-Authorization` header incorrectly, resulting in the value being
  sent through the tunneled connection to the destination server. Users who rely on
  defining their proxy credentials in the URL are *strongly* encouraged to upgrade
  to Requests 2.31.0+ to prevent unintentional leakage and rotate their proxy
  credentials once the change has been fully deployed.

  Users who do not use a proxy or do not supply their proxy credentials through
  the user information portion of their proxy URL are not subject to this
  vulnerability.

  Full details can be read in our [Github Security Advisory](https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q)
  and [CVE-2023-32681](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-32681).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.30.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Dependencies**
- ⚠️ Added support for urllib3 2.0. ⚠️

  This may contain minor breaking changes so we advise careful testing and
  reviewing https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/v2-migration-guide.html
  prior to upgrading.

  Users who wish to stay on urllib3 1.x can pin to `urllib3<2`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.29.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Improvements**

- Requests now defers chunked requests to the urllib3 implementation to improve
  standardization. (6226)
- Requests relaxes header component requirements to support bytes/str subclasses. (6356)
   ```
   
  
</details>

  - Changelog: https://data.safetycli.com/changelogs/requests/
  - Docs: https://requests.readthedocs.io
</details>

author: copilot
body:
This PR completely modernizes the theme system to provide a consistent, maintainable approach to styling across the entire workspace. The changes address the recurring CSS patterns and variable inconsistencies that were making the codebase difficult to maintain, while implementing an advanced host binding system for better DOM cascade control.

## Problem Statement

The existing theme system suffered from several issues:
- Inconsistent CSS variable naming (`--accent` vs `--accent-color`, `--foreground` vs `--foreground-color`)
- Commented out CSS variable generation in the theme service (lines 121-200 were disabled)
- Duplicate theme services between `libs/theme-ui` and `apps/client-interface`
- Hardcoded spacing, shadows, and design values throughout components
- No predefined color palettes - only single color generation
- Repetitive CSS patterns that could be abstracted into utility classes
- Poor DOM cascade handling in host bindings causing override conflicts

## Solution Overview

### 🎨 Enhanced Theme Service
- **8 Predefined Color Palettes**: Beautiful, carefully crafted color schemes including Optimistic Blue, Electric Sunset, Forest Dream, Cyberpunk Neon, Royal Purple, Ocean Breeze, Retro Gaming, and Minimal Monochrome
- **Restored CSS Variable Generation**: Previously commented out code now fully functional
- **Palette Mode Support**: Switch between predefined palettes or custom color selection
- **Proper Theme Persistence**: Enhanced storage to remember palette preferences
- **Automatic Global Variable Management**: Theme service now handles all CSS variable updates

### 🔧 Standardized CSS Variables
All theme variables now follow a consistent naming convention:

```css
/* Primary Colors */
--accent, --complement, --tertiary, --success, --danger, --warning

/* Numbered Shade System (0-9, lighter to darker) */
--accent-0 through --accent-9

/* Design Tokens */
--spacing-xs through --spacing-xxl (4px to 48px)
--shadow-sm through --shadow-xl
--border-radius-sm through --border-radius-xl
--font-size-xs through --font-size-xxl
--z-index-base through --z-index-overlay
```

### 🎯 Enhanced Host Binding System
- **Local Variable Pattern**: Components use `--local-*` prefixed variables for proper cascade control
- **CSS Fallback Chain**: `var(--local-accent, var(--accent, #fallback))` pattern prevents conflicts
- **DOM Override Support**: Child components inherit parent overrides without affecting siblings
- **ThemeHostBindingsDirective**: Advanced directive for complex host binding scenarios
- **ThemeVariableService**: Helper service for programmatic CSS variable management

### 🚀 New Components & Features
- **PaletteSelectorComponent**: Interactive UI for theme and palette selection
- **ThemeDemoComponent**: Comprehensive demonstration of new system capabilities
- **Comprehensive Utility Classes**: CSS utilities for spacing, colors, shadows, and common patterns
- **Design Token System**: Standardized values for consistent spacing and typography
- **Storybook Integration**: Visual demonstration of the theme system

### 🧹 Code Modernization
- **Updated All Components**: 15+ components migrated to new host binding pattern including Card, Button, Form components, Auth components, Blog components, and Chat components
- **Removed Duplicates**: Eliminated redundant theme service from client-interface
- **Migration from Hardcoded Values**: Replaced magic numbers with semantic design tokens
- **Enhanced Developer Experience**: Clear documentation and migration guide
- **App-Level Improvements**: Removed manual CSS variable setting, now use predefined palettes

## Key Benefits

1. **Consistency**: All components use the same variable naming convention
2. **Maintainability**: Design changes propagate automatically through CSS variables
3. **Flexibility**: Easy switching between 8 predefined palettes or custom colors
4. **Performance**: Efficient CSS variable updates without component re-renders
5. **Developer Productivity**: Utility classes and design tokens accelerate development
6. **Cascade Control**: Local overrides work properly without affecting other components
7. **Zero Conflicts**: Component-level customizations don't interfere with global theme

## Example Usage

```typescript
// Set a predefined palette
themeService.setPalette('Electric Sunset');

// New host binding pattern with local variables
@Component({
  host: {
    '[style.--local-accent]': 'accent',
    '[style.--local-complement]': 'complement',
  }
})

// Use standardized variables in component styles with fallback chain
.my-component {
  background-color: var(--local-background, var(--background, #ffffff));
  color: var(--local-foreground, var(--foreground, #212121));
  padding: var(--spacing-md);
  border-radius: var(--border-radius-lg);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-md);
}
```

## Testing
- ✅ All existing tests pass (theme-ui, common-ui, form-ui, auth-ui, blogging-ui, chat-ui)
- ✅ Theme switching works correctly
- ✅ Palette selection functions properly
- ✅ CSS variables generate as expected
- ✅ Local variable cascade working perfectly
- ✅ Component host binding migrations successful
- ✅ Client-interface builds successfully

## Migration Documentation

Complete migration guides and documentation provided:
- `HOST_BINDING_MIGRATION.md`: Step-by-step component migration guide
- `THEME_SYSTEM.md`: Full system documentation
- Interactive demo component showcasing all features

The theme system is now fully streamlined with enterprise-grade CSS variable management, proper DOM cascade control, and zero conflicts between component-level customizations.

author: cadiac
body:
## Summary

The query we used to determine data table sizes on sqlite was too slow on real life databases with unrelated execution/workflow data in other tables. The main reason seems to be the `LIKE data_table_user_%` part of the query, which forces a full table scan when getting just the data table's sizes.

With a subquery the query is way faster on instances with lots of other data, hopefully solving our `/data-tables-global/limits` endpoint's performance issues on `1.113.0` cloud.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

author: alfredbrannare
body:
## Description
Dependency Injection lab demonstrating three approaches to managing object dependencies in Java:
For assignment #95 

1. **Manual Constructor Injection** - Creating objects manually and passing dependencies through constructors
2. **Simple DI Container** - Built a simple container that automatically resolves dependencies using reflection
3. **Weld CDI** - Added Weld as an example with annotations for automatic dependency management

## Implementation
- Created `MessageService` and `MessageRepository` interfaces with multiple implementations
- `SimpleDIContainer` handles class registration and dependency resolution
- Added CDI annotations (`@ApplicationScoped`, `@Inject`) and custom qualifiers (`@InMemory`, `@Database`)
- Each approach shows different levels of automation and complexity

author: copilot
body:
Transformed the basic GitHub Pages placeholder into a complete, professional website for Lillebælt Bouldering Club. The new website provides all essential information and functionality needed for a climbing club community.

## Changes Made

### Complete Website Structure
- **Hero Section**: Eye-catching welcome area with club branding and call-to-action
- **About Section**: Three key features highlighting the club's inclusive community, indoor/outdoor activities, and strong social bonds
- **Bouldering Education**: Informational section explaining what bouldering is for newcomers
- **Events & Activities**: Details about weekly meetups, outdoor trips, and competitions
- **Membership Benefits**: Information about gym discounts, training programs, and social events
- **Contact Information**: Multiple contact methods including email, social media, and meetup location

### Technical Improvements
- **Responsive Design**: Added comprehensive CSS with mobile-first approach
- **Modern Styling**: Professional color scheme with gradients, shadows, and smooth animations
- **Navigation**: Fixed header with smooth scrolling navigation between sections
- **SEO Optimization**: Proper meta tags, descriptions, and semantic HTML structure
- **Accessibility**: Proper heading hierarchy and semantic markup

### Club-Specific Content
- Danish climbing community focus with local references
- Specific meetup details: Kolding Climbing Center, Wednesdays 7:00-9:00 PM
- Professional contact information: info@lillebaeltbouldering.dk
- Social media presence: @lillebaeltbouldering
- Comprehensive information for both beginners and experienced climbers

### Files Added/Modified
- **index.html**: Complete redesign from basic template to full website
- **styles.css**: New comprehensive stylesheet with responsive design
- **.gitignore**: Added to exclude temporary and build files

**Desktop View:**

immich-app/immich (ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning) ### [`v1.143.0`](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/releases/tag/v1.143.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/compare/v1.142.1...v1.143.0) ##### v1.143.0 > \[!NOTE] > *If you're still experiencing issues with remote assets or albums not showing up on the mobile app, please ensure that your server is updated to the latest version. If you are still having issues, try logging out and back in.* ##### Highlights Welcome to release `v1.143.0` of Immich. Like all releases, this one includes the latest batch of translations. A special thanks to everyone who has contributed so far to translating the project. If you are interested in helping translate yourself, check out our project on [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/immich/immich/). Other than that, this release is *mostly* bug fixes, with a few minor enhancements. Now let’s dive right in! - Material 3 switch/toggle (web) [#​22100](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22100) - Bring back configurable backup settings (mobile) [#​22114](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22114) - Concurrent hashing & hashing progress (mobile) [#​21997](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/21997) - Download progress (mobile) [#​22178](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22178) - Notable fix: Web modals [#​22079](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22079) - Notable fix: Mobile “freezes” [#​22111](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22111) - Notable fix: Copy image on Safari ##### Material 3 switch/toggle (web) The web project has an updated switch/toggle, thanks to [@​SevereCloud](https://redirect.github.com/SevereCloud) ([immich-app/ui#267](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/ui/pull/267)) for that. ##### Bring back configurable backup settings (Android) Just like the previous timeline implementation, the new version now has similar settings for - Backup only while charging - Upload only after a minimum amount of elapsed time ##### Concurrent hashing & hashing progress (mobile) Improvements have been made to the client-side hashing implementation, which now enables hashing to happen *concurrently*. This significantly increases throughput, and now the speed is mostly limited by how fast files can be read from internal storage. The hashing process has also been updated to only hash assets from the albums selected for backups, which reduces the number of downloads for iCloud users. ##### Download progress (mobile) The mobile app now has a built-in download progress indicator, which makes it easy to see the progress of files being downloaded onto the device.

##### Notable fix: Web modals Previous to this release, the web application would often “freeze” or become unusable after using a modal (creating a shared link, creating an api key, confirming the deletion of assets, etc.). This issue has been fixed. ##### Notable fix: Mobile “freezes” This release fixes an issue that the mobile application could occasionally “freeze”, with the thumbnails would stop loading, and certain pages would become unusable until the application was forced closed. This has proved much more challenging to solve. We determined that the cause was due to concurrent access to SQLite from background/foreground processes, which could have put the app into this state. We have taken measures to address these situations and believe the application should be much more *stable*. If you are still running into these types of issues, please let us know! ##### Notable fix: Copy image on Safari The “copy image to clipboard” functionality has long worked on non-Safari browsers, but in this release, we were finally able to identify and implement a fix. Copying an image to the clipboard should now also work on Safari. ##### Support Immich

author: elalemanyo
body:
## Summary

This PR adds environment variable control for debug mode in the ReActionView install generator, allowing any developer to disable debug mode in their own environment without modifying code.

## Changes

- Modified the debug_mode configuration in the install generator to check both `Rails.env.development?` and the absence of the `REACTIONVIEW_DISABLE_DEBUG_MODE` environment variable.
- Debug mode is now enabled only when both conditions are true:
  1. Rails environment is development
  2. `REACTIONVIEW_DISABLE_DEBUG_MODE environment variable is not set (defaults to enabled)

## Motivation

Previously, debug mode was hardcoded to be enabled in all development environments. This change allows individual developers to control debug mode through their own environment setup without touching any application code. Each developer can now:
- Set their own preference via environment variables
- Disable debug mode when it's not needed for their workflow
- Avoid modifying shared configuration files
- Have personalized development environments

## Backward Compatibility

✅ This change is fully backward compatible. Debug mode remains enabled by default in development environments, preserving existing behavior unless a developer explicitly chooses to disable it.

## Usage

Any developer can disable debug mode in their environment by setting the environment variable to any value:

```bash
export REACTIONVIEW_DISABLE_DEBUG_MODE=1
# or
export REACTIONVIEW_DISABLE_DEBUG_MODE=true
# or
export REACTIONVIEW_DISABLE_DEBUG_MODE=yes
```

No code changes required - just personal environment configuration!

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete Single Page Application (SPA) for couples to manage their tasks collaboratively, following all the specified requirements. The application is built using React functional components, Tailwind CSS, and stores all data in LocalStorage without requiring any backend services.

![Complete SPA Implementation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/decdb51e-ee48-4728-95de-4bdbbae43411)

## Key Features Implemented

### Enhanced Priority System
- **Extended priority levels**: A1-A3 (urgent & important), B1-B3 (important but less urgent), C1-C3 (nice to do), and D (can be postponed)
- **Visual hierarchy**: Each priority level has distinct colors and emojis for quick identification
- **Smart sorting**: Tasks are automatically sorted by priority throughout the application

### Assignment & Collaboration
- **Three assignment types**: "Me", "Partner", and "Both" with distinct visual indicators
- **Color coding**: Default pink for "Me", blue for "Partner", and gradient combinations for "Both"
- **User customization**: Color picker for personalizing "Me" task colors
- **Partner connection**: Invite code system for linking accounts and sharing tasks

### Comprehensive Task Management
- **Full CRUD operations**: Create, read, update, and delete tasks with rich metadata
- **Flexible scheduling**: Optional day of week and time selection
- **Drag-and-drop calendar**: Move tasks between days using @dnd-kit
- **Click-to-scroll**: Tasks in Today's section scroll to their calendar position when clicked

### AI-Powered Task Import
- **Static AI prompt**: Pre-formatted prompt for external AI assistants at the bottom of the page
- **Intelligent parsing**: Handles complex task formats like `[A1] Task description (assigned to: Me) [Monday, 9:00 AM]`
- **Batch import**: Uses `---` delimiters to separate multiple tasks
- **Automatic scheduling**: Imported tasks are placed on correct calendar days

### ADHD-Friendly Design
- **Clear visual hierarchy**: Important tasks stand out with proper color coding and urgency indicators
- **Progress tracking**: Completion percentages and visual progress bars
- **Jarvis integration**: Helpful AI-style commentary and productivity tips
- **Gentle animations**: Smooth transitions without being distracting

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **React 19** with modern hooks (useState, useEffect, useContext)
- **TypeScript interfaces** for type safety
- **Context-based state management** for auth and tasks
- **Modular component structure** ready for mobile app expansion

### Data Persistence
- **LocalStorage integration** with automatic JSON serialization
- **Invite code system** for simulating partner data sharing
- **Persistent user preferences** including custom colors

### Layout Structure
1. **Top Section**: Today's Tasks with priority-based sorting and completion tracking
2. **Middle Section**: Task creation form and partner management with color settings
3. **Bottom Section**: 7-column weekly calendar (Monday-Sunday) with drag-and-drop
4. **Footer**: AI prompt display and Jarvis productivity wisdom

## User Experience Highlights

- **Immediate feedback**: Tasks appear instantly in both Today's section and calendar
- **Smart defaults**: Reasonable priority levels and assignments for quick task creation
- **Mobile responsive**: Works seamlessly on both desktop and mobile devices
- **Error handling**: Graceful handling of edge cases and user input validation

This implementation provides a solid foundation for future expansion into a mobile app using Capacitor or React Native, with clean separation of concerns and reusable components.

author: angelogiacco
body: Correct `opKindToDir` function logic to accurately map publish/subscribe operations to incoming/outgoing types, resolving sporadic linter failures caused by malformed generated types. The previous `opKindToDir` function had incorrect mappings for client-side publish/subscribe and server-side publish/subscribe operations, leading to generated types being placed in the wrong `incoming.ts` or `outgoing.ts` files. This inconsistency caused intermittent syntax errors during the type generation and compilation steps. The fix ensures that types are correctly categorized based on their direction relative to the client or server role. --- [Slack Thread](https://eleven-labs-workspace.slack.com/archives/D094A2U16DS/p1758571282752349?thread_ts=1758571282.752349&cid=D094A2U16DS)

author: szzazi
body:
This pull request introduces a new "sync-only" mode to the backup script, allowing users to sync files directly to the remote share without creating a zip archive. The sync-only behavior can be set as the default in the configuration, and the installer has been enhanced to support this and other configuration improvements. The documentation and user experience have also been updated to reflect these changes.

**Sync-only mode and configuration:**

* Added support for a `--sync-only` CLI flag in `startBackup.sh`, enabling users to sync a specified folder (or all folders in `SOURCE_DIRS_LIST` if no path is given) directly to the remote share without zipping. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ec1ae6f5776cbf2fe6ae6bcb5b6f79697df78996e652f73353041ae5311d0ceR19-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ec1ae6f5776cbf2fe6ae6bcb5b6f79697df78996e652f73353041ae5311d0ceR31-R32) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7ec1ae6f5776cbf2fe6ae6bcb5b6f79697df78996e652f73353041ae5311d0ceR60-R69) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7ec1ae6f5776cbf2fe6ae6bcb5b6f79697df78996e652f73353041ae5311d0ceR165-R225)
* Introduced `SYNC_ONLY_DEFAULT` in `config.conf` to control whether the script runs in sync-only mode by default. This can be set during installation via `configure.sh`, and is documented in `README.md` and `config.conf.example`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R92-R104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fd1519f6e656bc790f196c745c5d24a0dcfb205298e18305bf06a819a160cc43R62-R65) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba17b1855b0f97042c31b2b2c2fd2b075fa355a840b152f1959daf2a755266eL35-R112)
* The script now checks both CLI and config values to determine whether to run in sync-only mode, with CLI taking precedence.

**Installer and configuration improvements:**

* The installer (`configure.sh`) now loads existing config values and pre-fills prompts with current settings, including for MySQL and Samba options. It also prompts for the new sync-only default. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba17b1855b0f97042c31b2b2c2fd2b075fa355a840b152f1959daf2a755266eR12-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba17b1855b0f97042c31b2b2c2fd2b075fa355a840b152f1959daf2a755266eL35-R112) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba17b1855b0f97042c31b2b2c2fd2b075fa355a840b152f1959daf2a755266eL205-R263)
* Improved cron job setup in `configure.sh` for robustness, and added clear post-install notes and examples for sync-only usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba17b1855b0f97042c31b2b2c2fd2b075fa355a840b152f1959daf2a755266eR239-R244) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba17b1855b0f97042c31b2b2c2fd2b075fa355a840b152f1959daf2a755266eR275-R282)

**Documentation updates:**

* Updated `README.md` to document the sync-only mode, configuration options, usage examples, and how the new behavior works with or without CLI flags. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R92-R104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R228-R241)

These changes make the backup script more flexible and user-friendly, especially for users who want to sync files without archiving them.

### Description and Notes

This PR removes the log file read ports and the unnecessary parallelism of multiple Python programs running for each task. Originally, I wanted to implement pytest, but instead, I started by refactoring the test_runner.py to solve the parallelism issue. After that, I started implementing pytest in the example tests. You can run it with: "uv run pytest tests/example/* ". You can set "-n auto" for multithread.

The original framework has some problems - we were basically building our own testing framework from scratch, which meant constantly fixing bugs and adding features that already exist elsewhere. Plus, we kept getting random failures when reading log files. When the files got too big, the test would just  timeout. 

With pytest, we get all the standard testing features, multithread support, proper logging, and tons of configuration options in pyproject.toml. The documentation is solid and there's a huge ecosystem of plugins. Makes way more sense to use this instead of spending time on our custom solution.

Now we can focus on what actually matters - node management and the tests themselves. Plus, the test code is way cleaner and simpler now.

author: erichkeane
body:
After previous implementation, I discovered that we were both doing arrays incorrectly for recipes, plus didn't get the pointer allocations done correctly.  This patch is the first of a few in a series that attempts to make sure we get all pointers/arrays correct.

This patch is limited to just 'private' and destructors, which simplifies the review significantly. Destructors are simply looped through and called at each level.

The 'recipe-decl' is the 'least bounded' (that is, the type of the
    expression, in the type of `int[5] i; #pragma acc parallel
    private(i[1])`, the type of the `recipe-decl` is `int`.  This allows
    us to do init/destruction at the element level.

This patch also adds infrastructure for the rest of the series of private (for the init section), as well as extensive testing for 'private', with a lot of 'TODO' locations.

Future patches will fill these in, but at the moment, there is an NYI warning for bounds, so a number of tests are updated to handle that.

immich-app/immich (ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning) ### [`v1.143.0`](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/releases/tag/v1.143.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/compare/v1.142.1...v1.143.0) ##### v1.143.0 > \[!NOTE] > *If you're still experiencing issues with remote assets or albums not showing up on the mobile app, please ensure that your server is updated to the latest version. If you are still having issues, try logging out and back in.* ##### Highlights Welcome to release `v1.143.0` of Immich. Like all releases, this one includes the latest batch of translations. A special thanks to everyone who has contributed so far to translating the project. If you are interested in helping translate yourself, check out our project on [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/immich/immich/). Other than that, this release is *mostly* bug fixes, with a few minor enhancements. Now let’s dive right in! - Material 3 switch/toggle (web) [#​22100](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22100) - Bring back configurable backup settings (mobile) [#​22114](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22114) - Concurrent hashing & hashing progress (mobile) [#​21997](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/21997) - Download progress (mobile) [#​22178](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22178) - Notable fix: Web modals [#​22079](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22079) - Notable fix: Mobile “freezes” [#​22111](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22111) - Notable fix: Copy image on Safari ##### Material 3 switch/toggle (web) The web project has an updated switch/toggle, thanks to [@​SevereCloud](https://redirect.github.com/SevereCloud) ([immich-app/ui#267](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/ui/pull/267)) for that. ##### Bring back configurable backup settings (Android) Just like the previous timeline implementation, the new version now has similar settings for - Backup only while charging - Upload only after a minimum amount of elapsed time ##### Concurrent hashing & hashing progress (mobile) Improvements have been made to the client-side hashing implementation, which now enables hashing to happen *concurrently*. This significantly increases throughput, and now the speed is mostly limited by how fast files can be read from internal storage. The hashing process has also been updated to only hash assets from the albums selected for backups, which reduces the number of downloads for iCloud users. ##### Download progress (mobile) The mobile app now has a built-in download progress indicator, which makes it easy to see the progress of files being downloaded onto the device.

##### Notable fix: Web modals Previous to this release, the web application would often “freeze” or become unusable after using a modal (creating a shared link, creating an api key, confirming the deletion of assets, etc.). This issue has been fixed. ##### Notable fix: Mobile “freezes” This release fixes an issue that the mobile application could occasionally “freeze”, with the thumbnails would stop loading, and certain pages would become unusable until the application was forced closed. This has proved much more challenging to solve. We determined that the cause was due to concurrent access to SQLite from background/foreground processes, which could have put the app into this state. We have taken measures to address these situations and believe the application should be much more *stable*. If you are still running into these types of issues, please let us know! ##### Notable fix: Copy image on Safari The “copy image to clipboard” functionality has long worked on non-Safari browsers, but in this release, we were finally able to identify and implement a fix. If you are interested in helping translate yourself, check out our project on [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/immich/immich/). Other than that, this release is *mostly* bug fixes, with a few minor enhancements. Now let’s dive right in! - Material 3 switch/toggle (web) [#​22100](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22100) - Bring back configurable backup settings (mobile) [#​22114](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22114) - Concurrent hashing & hashing progress (mobile) [#​21997](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/21997) - Download progress (mobile) [#​22178](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22178) - Notable fix: Web modals [#​22079](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22079) - Notable fix: Mobile “freezes” [#​22111](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/22111) - Notable fix: Copy image on Safari ##### Material 3 switch/toggle (web) The web project has an updated switch/toggle, thanks to [@​SevereCloud](https://redirect.github.com/SevereCloud) ([immich-app/ui#267](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/ui/pull/267)) for that. ##### Bring back configurable backup settings (Android) Just like the previous timeline implementation, the new version now has similar settings for - Backup only while charging - Upload only after a minimum amount of elapsed time ##### Concurrent hashing & hashing progress (mobile) Improvements have been made to the client-side hashing implementation, which now enables hashing to happen *concurrently*. This significantly increases throughput, and now the speed is mostly limited by how fast files can be read from internal storage. The hashing process has also been updated to only hash assets from the albums selected for backups, which reduces the number of downloads for iCloud users. ##### Download progress (mobile) The mobile app now has a built-in download progress indicator, which makes it easy to see the progress of files being downloaded onto the device.

##### Notable fix: Web modals Previous to this release, the web application would often “freeze” or become unusable after using a modal (creating a shared link, creating an api key, confirming the deletion of assets, etc.). This issue has been fixed. ##### Notable fix: Mobile “freezes” This release fixes an issue that the mobile application could occasionally “freeze”, with the thumbnails would stop loading, and certain pages would become unusable until the application was forced closed. This has proved much more challenging to solve. We determined that the cause was due to concurrent access to SQLite from background/foreground processes, which could have put the app into this state. We have taken measures to address these situations and believe the application should be much more *stable*. If you are still running into these types of issues, please let us know! ##### Notable fix: Copy image on Safari The “copy image to clipboard” functionality has long worked on non-Safari browsers, but in this release, we were finally able to identify and implement a fix. body:
This pull request introduces a new revenue overview feature for admin order statistics, updating both the backend (API and services) and the frontend dashboard. The main changes include adding a new API endpoint to fetch revenue data, calculating revenue and lost revenue on the backend, and updating the frontend to display this information dynamically.

**Backend: Revenue Overview Feature**

* Added a new API endpoint `/admin/orders/revenue/{period}` that returns revenue statistics for a given period, including total revenue, lost revenue, and monthly comparison. (`app/routes/admin_orders.py`, `app/schemas/admin.py`, `app/services/admin_overview_services.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-776cdcae0e41644741e5b2143eea163b0b612131bb3af687c0bf6362469362d9L4-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-776cdcae0e41644741e5b2143eea163b0b612131bb3af687c0bf6362469362d9R20-R23) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-066a7a8572023aa1556af3a92a1e392ea1ee8a67080673f01712b297c69252fdR52-R58) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-67ed9482b1e9fad36e47c2580720ca0d4746d74ac688c19969ce20933409db57R122-R197)
* Implemented the `get_revenue_overview` service, which calculates total and lost revenue by iterating over orders, cart items, and products, and computes the percentage change compared to the previous month. (`app/services/admin_overview_services.py`)

**Frontend: Revenue Overview Integration**

* Updated the `OrderStatsCards` component to fetch and display revenue statistics, including total revenue, lost revenue, and monthly change, based on the selected period. author: filipelautert
body:
This pull request updates the documentation and licensing files for Liquibase Community 5.0, reflecting major changes in product packaging, dependency management, and support options. The documentation now emphasizes the modular nature of Liquibase Community, introduces the integrated Liquibase Package Manager (LPM), and clarifies example project formats. Additionally, a new open source license file has been added.

**Documentation updates:**

* Updated `GETTING_STARTED.TXT` and `README.txt` to highlight that Liquibase Community 5.0 ships without extensions, drivers, or extra dependencies, making it lighter and more customizable for users. The docs now instruct users to manage dependencies via the integrated Liquibase Package Manager (`liquibase lpm`), and provide links to LPM documentation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ca70b21d9d5e2f524cfbe066d211c452dfef4fb5a5c14a2972190398bcfd9d20L1-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f30b1f2cc4b283bb2ab559924d51845d8ca8d4367969ad6d01e78aab5ab4c394L1-R38)
* Expanded the examples section to include new changelog formats (`json` and `yaml`), updating instructions and references throughout the documentation to reflect these additions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ca70b21d9d5e2f524cfbe066d211c452dfef4fb5a5c14a2972190398bcfd9d20R30-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ca70b21d9d5e2f524cfbe066d211c452dfef4fb5a5c14a2972190398bcfd9d20L120-R123) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ca70b21d9d5e2f524cfbe066d211c452dfef4fb5a5c14a2972190398bcfd9d20L142-R145) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f30b1f2cc4b283bb2ab559924d51845d8ca8d4367969ad6d01e78aab5ab4c394L1-R38)
* Improved clarity and accuracy in installation instructions, directory structure, and file descriptions for both Windows and Mac installations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f30b1f2cc4b283bb2ab559924d51845d8ca8d4367969ad6d01e78aab5ab4c394L1-R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f30b1f2cc4b283bb2ab559924d51845d8ca8d4367969ad6d01e78aab5ab4c394L43-R79)

**Licensing and support:**

* Added a new open source license file `FSL-1.1-ALv2.txt` describing the Functional Source License and future transition to Apache License 2.0.
* Updated support information to direct users to Liquibase Pro for enterprise support and clarified community support channels (Stack Overflow, forum, docs). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ca70b21d9d5e2f524cfbe066d211c452dfef4fb5a5c14a2972190398bcfd9d20L250-R259) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f30b1f2cc4b283bb2ab559924d51845d8ca8d4367969ad6d01e78aab5ab4c394L43-R79)

**Other improvements:**

* Updated copyright notices to 2025 and standardized formatting across documentation files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ca70b21d9d5e2f524cfbe066d211c452dfef4fb5a5c14a2972190398bcfd9d20L250-R259) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f30b1f2cc4b283bb2ab559924d51845d8ca8d4367969ad6d01e78aab5ab4c394L43-R79)

## Description

Updated OSS distribution documentation and licensing to align with Liquibase 5.0 updates. Highlights include:

# What

:green_circle: This backwards-compatible changeset for patch version `v0.2.5`...
* Adds new...
  * Reusable Workflow `delete_docker_hub_repositories.yml`
  * Underlying `Dockerfile`-based `action` to delete the specified Docker Hub repositories
* Adds new Reusable Workflow `latest_tag.yml` for specifying the project's latest tag
* Adds `repository` `output`s to the `image-names` Reusable workflow...
  * `dev_repository`
  * `unvetted_repository`
  * `vetted_repository`

The Reusable Workflow `delete_docker_hub_repositories.yml` accepts and deletes a list of Docker Hub repositories (i.e. image names without the tag) (specified as a JSON array represented as a string).

The  `Dockerfile`-based `action` `delete-docker-hub-repository` deletes a single Docker Hub repository **names** (i.e. `gh-actions-test-bed_dev-add-action-delete-docker-hub-repo-dev`) matching the Docker Hub API.

# Change Impact Analysis and Testing
These changes are additive other than the modifications to the existing PR workflow file to verify the new `image-names` and `latest_tag` `output`s.  Those new verifications and their inspection will verify the new `latest_tag` workflow and new `output`s.

The development and testing of the new Reusable Workflow and `action` to delete the Docker Hub repositories was done with the related testing PRs used to test the deletion during PR workflows in development and on merge with the intended pattern...
*  brianjbayer/gh-actions-test-bed#58
*  brianjbayer/gh-actions-test-bed#59

The intended pattern of deletion was then copied into this PR but that can only be executes on Merge.

- [x] Successful PR Checks of this PR and their inspection verifies the new `repository` `output`s to the `image-names` Reusable workflow and mitigates risk of regressions

- [x] Successful PR and [Merge Checks](https://github.com/brianjbayer/gh-actions-test-bed/actions/runs/18250362805) of related PR and their inspection verifies these new changes work as expected in other repositories and that there are no regressions.

author: othakkar
body:
This PR enables support for oneDNN Layer-Norm operations in the XLA:CPU Thunk runtime, building upon the foundational implementation of `OneDnnOpThunk`.

Key changes:
- Updated thunk emitter to emit `OneDnnOpThunk` for oneDNN layer-norm during compilation.
- Re-enable the custom call rewrite to oneDNN layer-norm in `onednn_ops_rewriter.cc`.
- Added support for oneDNN Layer-Norm op via `ExecuteOneDnnLayerNorm(...)` in `onednn_layer_norm.cc`.

body:
:warning: These fixes were AI generated and human tested. There is a real chance the new normalization and ignoring mobs in group 0 could have other consequences I'm not aware of.

That said, it worked and I was able to get updated mobdb files now.

I'm not currently confident enough to try submitting this to Thorny's repo, so it'll sit against my fork until that changes, but of course go ahead and submit it yourself if you find this and like it. 

---
## FFXI Mob Database Import Script Improvements

### Summary

Enhanced the mob database import script to significantly improve success rates and provide better error diagnostics.

### Key Changes

 **🔧 Fixed Major Issue: Missing Pool Data**

- **Root Cause**: Script was processing groups with PoolId = 0 (unimplemented/disabled mobs)
- **Fix**: Skip groups with PoolId = 0 during group building phase
- **Impact**: Eliminates ~8,000 "Missing Pool Data" errors

**🎯 Enhanced Name Matching Algorithm**

- **Problem**: Strict matching missed valid variants like Eo'zdei vs Eozdei_Still
- **Solution**: Added fuzzy matching with normalization for:
  - Apostrophes (' → removed)
  - Question marks (??? → qm)
  - Spaces and underscores (normalized)
  - Suffix variants (_Still, _Fast, _qm)
- **Impact**: Catches previously failed name matches

**📊 Improved Error Reporting**

- Added structured error categorization:
  - DAT Name Mismatches
  - Missing DAT Data
  - Missing Group Data
  - Missing Pool Data
  - Other Errors
- Enhanced output format with clear breakdown
- Removed debug spam (monster: table: 0x...)

### Results

**Before**: Success: 76,388 | Failure: 8,748 (Missing Pool Data: 8,031)
**Expected**: Dramatic reduction in failures with ~8,000 fewer missing pool errors

author: cosmir17
body:
## Summary
Testing the fork-friendly Checkmarx solution from PM-19431. This updates our workflow to allow fork PRs to run security scans without requiring access to secrets.

## Problem
Fork PRs currently fail Checkmarx scans because they cannot access repository secrets (GitHub security feature). This blocks external contributions.

## Solution
Using the new `checkmarx-scan-public` action with `pull_request_target`:
- Changed from `pull_request` to `pull_request_target` event
- Removed main code checkout (critical for security)
- Checkmarx fetches code directly from repo URL

## Changes
- Modified `.github/workflows/checkmarx.yaml`:
  - Event: `pull_request` → `pull_request_target`
  - Removed main code checkout step
  - Uses new `checkmarx-scan-public` action

## Security
- `pull_request_target` runs with base branch context (has secrets)
- No code checkout means no risk of running untrusted code
- Safe for fork PRs

## Dependencies
⚠️ **Requires**: midnightntwrk/upload-sarif-github-action#25 to be merged first

## Testing
Once both PRs are merged:
1. Create a fork of midnight-node-docker
2. Submit a test PR from the fork
3. Verify Checkmarx scan runs successfully

## References
- PM-19431: Fork-friendly Checkmarx solution
- PM-19178: Original issue about fork PRs failing

cc @gilescope

It sounds like `SimpleExecutor` was a temporary solution to "sync points" in schedules, but now those can be inferred, so `SimpleExecutor` is unnecessary now.

Further, `SimpleExecutor` and `SingleThreadedExecutor` were *very* similar, which was becoming a consistency and code quality headache.

## Solution

Remove `SimpleExecutor`.

author: copilot
body:
Cette PR implémente plusieurs améliorations demandées pour l'interface utilisateur et corrige les problèmes de compression Ghostscript qui causaient des erreurs de code 255.

## Changements principaux

### Interface utilisateur améliorée
- **Renommage du champ "Profondeur" en "Couleurs"** pour une meilleure clarté
- **Nouvelles options de couleurs** avec des descriptions plus explicites :
  - `"1 bit (N&B)"` → `"Noir & Blanc (1bit)"`
  - `"8 bits (256 niveaux)"` → `"Niveaux de gris (8 bits)"`
  - `"24 bits (16M couleurs)"` → `"Couleurs (24 bits)"`
- Mise à jour des tooltips avec la nouvelle terminologie

### Profils de conversion par défaut mis à jour
Les profils par défaut ont été ajustés selon les spécifications :
- **"Fax G4"** : 150 DPI (au lieu de 200), compression G4, Noir & Blanc
- **"Niveaux de gris"** : 150 DPI (au lieu de 300), compression LZW, Niveaux de gris
- **"Couleurs"** : 150 DPI (au lieu de 300), compression LZW, Couleurs

### Correction du code d'erreur 255 de Ghostscript
Le problème avec les compressions PackBits, ZIP et JPEG a été résolu :
- Amélioration de la gestion des paramètres de compression dans `GhostscriptRunner.cs`
- Meilleur formatage des paramètres pour différents types de compression
- Gestion appropriée des cas de compression nulle/aucune

### Filtrage dynamique des compressions
Implémentation d'un système intelligent qui adapte les options de compression selon le type de couleur sélectionné :

- **Noir & Blanc** : Affiche uniquement G3, G4, LZW, ZIP, PackBits, Aucune (G4 par défaut)
- **Niveaux de gris** : Affiche LZW, ZIP, PackBits, JPEG, Aucune (LZW par défaut)
- **Couleurs** : Affiche LZW, ZIP, PackBits, JPEG, Aucune (LZW par défaut)

### Validation automatique
- Correction automatique des combinaisons incompatibles (ex: G4 avec couleurs)
- Messages d'avertissement conviviaux pour guider l'utilisateur
- Prévention des erreurs avant la conversion

## Impact technique

Ces changements améliorent significativement l'expérience utilisateur en :
- Empêchant les configurations invalides qui causaient des erreurs Ghostscript
- Rendant l'interface plus intuitive avec des termes français clairs
- Optimisant les paramètres par défaut pour un usage général (150 DPI)
- Maintenant la compatibilité ascendante avec les configurations existantes

Tous les changements ont été testés et le projet Core compile sans erreur.

⏺ Upgrades Performed Summary

  1. Ruby Version Upgrade

  - From: Ruby 3.1.3
  - To: Ruby 3.4.5
  - Files changed: .ruby-version, Gemfile

  2. Rails Framework Upgrade

  - From: Rails 7.0.6
  - To: Rails 8.0.3
  - Config changes:
    - Updated config.load_defaults from 7.0 to 8.0
    - Removed deprecated config.server_timing from development.rb
    - Added new Rails 8 configuration files via rails app:update

  3. Core Gem Upgrades

  | Gem    | From     | To       | Reason                  |
  |--------|----------|----------|-------------------------|
  | rails  | ~> 7.0.6 | ~> 8.0.0 | Main framework upgrade  |
  | puma   | ~> 5.0   | ~> 6.4   | Better Ruby 3.4 support |
  | pg     | ~> 1.1   | ~> 1.5   | Rails 8 compatibility   |
  | redis  | ~> 4.0   | ~> 5.0   | Rails 8 compatibility   |
  | pay    | ~> 6.0   | ~> 7.0   | Rails 8 support         |
  | stripe | 8.5.0    | ~> 12.0  | Required by Pay 7       |

  4. Removed Deprecated Gems

  - webdrivers - Removed (Selenium 4+ has built-in driver management)

  5. Code Refactors

  CheckoutController fixes:

  - Removed Pay gem's deprecated checkout method
  - Replaced with direct Stripe::Checkout::Session.create() calls
  - Fixed infinite recursion in URL helper methods
  - Added conditional customer handling for Stripe

  View updates:

  - Removed deprecated Pay gem partials (pay/stripe/checkout_button)
  - Updated checkout/show.html.erb and checkout/create.html.erb
  - Replaced with direct Stripe checkout URL redirect buttons

  6. Database Updates

  - Added Active Storage migrations for Rails 8
  - Created test database
  - Ran migrations successfully

  7. Configuration Restorations

  - Re-added Letter Opener mail configuration after rails app:update
  - Maintained Devise authentication settings
  - Preserved environment-specific configurations

  8. Compatibility Fixes

  - Fixed Rack 3.0 compatibility
  - Updated for new Redis client API
  - Resolved Pay 7 API changes
  - Fixed stack overflow errors in checkout flow

  All upgrades completed successfully with the application now running on Ruby 3.4.5 and Rails 8.0.3! 🎉
